"The Great War" is a song written and produced by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift for her tenth studio album, Midnights (2022). Produced by her and Aaron Dessner, "The Great War" is a folktronica track with influences of indie pop, accompanied by synthesizers. Lyrically, it references World War I as an analogy of a heartbreak as navigating a severe and turbulent conflict within a serious relationship.
"The Great War" was released as a bonus track in the 3am edition of Midnights. The song reached number 24 on the Billboard Global 200 and number 26 on the Billboard Hot 100.
Background and release
On October 21, 2022, American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift released her tenth original studio album, Midnights through Republic Records, exploring themes of self-doubt, heartbreak and conflicts. Three hours later, an extended version of the album was surprise-released – the 3am Edition, featuring seven bonus tracks including "The Great War". The song was also included in the album's Late Night Edition released less than a year later, on May 26, 2023.
Swift performed "The Great War" live for the first time in her sixth concert tour, "The Eras Tour" on April 14, 2023, during the Tampa, Florida stop, where she was accompanied by Aaron Dessner. It was performed for the second time on June 14, 2024 in Liverpool, England, mashed-up with "You're Losing Me". Swift later performed this song again for the last time on November 3, 2024, in Indianapolis, Indiana, paired with "Death by a Thousand Cuts".
Composition
Swift wrote "The Great War" with Aaron Dessner
Critical reception
Commercial performance
"The Great War" debuted and peaked at number 26 on the US Billboard Hot 100. On the Billboard Global 200, it peaked at number 24.
